quote.text: Those are the reflections you should recur to morning and night. Start with things that are least valuable and most liable to be lost – things such as a jug or a glass – and proceed to apply the same ideas to clothes, pets, livestock, property; then to yourself, your body, the body’s parts, your children, your siblings and your wife. [112] Look on every side and mentally discard them. Purify your thoughts, in case of an attachment or devotion to something that doesn’t belong to you and will hurt to have wrenched away. [113] And as you exercise daily, as you do at the gym, do not say that you are philosophizing (admittedly a pretentious claim), but that you are a slave presenting your emancipator;14 because this is genuine freedom that you cultivate.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Just as Epictetus advises us to let go of what is not truly ours, approach parenting by cherishing your children’s uniqueness without clinging to preconceived expectations, accepting that change is a natural part of growth.
    • Practice nurturing guidance and resilience by preparing your children to face life’s uncertainties, teaching them that while love endures, external circumstances and material things are fleeting.
  • Leadership
    • Embrace the freedom of detachment in leadership, letting go of the need to be overly attached to titles or possessions so you can make decisions based purely on what benefits the common good.
    • Cultivate a mindset of constant self-improvement and adaptation, recognizing that each resource or loyal support may eventually change, thereby requiring you to remain humble and flexible in your leadership approach.
  • Product Management
    • Apply the stoic principle of discarding what is nonessential to product management; strive to focus on delivering real value while being ready to abandon features or practices that no longer serve your users.
    • View each product iteration as a continuous exercise in refinement—by letting go of outdated processes and being willing to pivot, you nurture innovation and maintain a healthy detachment that breeds long-term success.
